subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Graphene: The Thinnest Material Ever Made
description: A short lesson to help you apply Graphene: The Thinnest Material Ever Made.

hook.text: Graphene is one atom thick. It's the strongest material ever tested — 200 times stronger than steel.

buildup.text: It's pure carbon arranged in a hexagonal lattice. Andre Geim isolated it in 2004 using sticky tape.

discovery.text: Graphene conducts electricity better than copper and heat better than diamond. It's nearly transparent.

twist.text: Despite two decades of research, graphene hasn't found a killer commercial application yet.

climax.text: Potential uses include flexible screens, water filters, and batteries that charge in seconds.

punchline.text: The wonder material is still looking for a job.

quiz.question: How did Andre Geim first isolate graphene in 2004?
options: He bombarded graphite with a laser to separate layers
He used sticky tape to peel off atom-thin layers from graphite
He dissolved graphite in acid and filtered the residue
